source_segments.text: The Great Depression curtailed many of the denomination ’ s activities , whether church-building campaigns , Sunday schools , or missions work .

World War II ( 1941-45 ) , however , once more resuscitated Lutheran communities , bringing another round of church founding during the 1950s and 1960s , particularly in Atlanta ’ s expanding suburbs .

By 1960 the American Lutheran Church had joined the synodical family of Georgia ’ s various Lutheran groups , and all together this assortment of synods maintained more than eighty churches in the state .
